transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-21 15:00 UTC — duration ~42m
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Romero (Redwood SE); Daniel Park (CISO, Aeon Medical), Maya Torres (Head of Infrastructure), Liam O'Neil (Product), Sana Rahman (Compliance)

Summary (auto): High-level security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Customer primarily evaluating Hosted + Dedicated but has strict data residency and encryption/KMS needs. Key concerns: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC granularity, audit logs retention and export, KMS/HSM integration, and data retention/erasure for medical PII. Next steps: send artifacts, schedule SE deep-dive on KMS and private deploy.

00:00:05 Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Jordan on the Redwood AE side, with Priya and Alex.
00:00:12 Daniel: Hi, Daniel Park, CISO at Aeon. We're looking at options for LLM features in our clinical workflows, and security is the blocker before we move to procurement.
00:00:24 Maya: Maya here, infra lead. We run on GCP primarily, VPC-first, some on-prem for legacy EHR connectors.
00:00:30 Liam: Liam, product — trying to understand latency/cost tradeoffs too.
00:00:35 Jordan: Great. Today we want to walk through Redwood's security posture, and map it to your requirements: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, encryption/KMS, and data retention. Feel free to stop and drill in.

00:01:10 Priya: Quick framing: Redwood has three deployment surfaces — Hosted (our managed API), Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity for a single customer), and Private (VPC or on-prem installs). Our security controls vary slightly by mode; we'll outline where data is processed, what controls we provide, and integration points for your KMS and SSO.
00:01:35 Daniel: Sounds good. Our baseline is we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence. Do you have active certs?
00:01:44 Jordan: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. We'll send the audit reports once NDA/LOU is completed. The hosted offering processes data in our managed clusters but we maintain strict tenant isolation and audit logs.
00:02:05 Sana: A couple follow-ups: for hosted — do you encrypt at rest with customer-managed keys or only platform-managed? And what about HSM?
00:02:14 Priya: By default hosted uses platform-managed encryption keys, but for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. For Dedicated in some clouds we can integrate with your KMS for at-rest encryption keys. For Private/on-prem we can use your HSM or bring-your-own KMS. Alex can share the integration patterns.
00:02:38 Alex: To add, for Dedicated we offer an option to use your KMS via Cloud KMS/CMK handshake — the runtime can be configured so that disk volumes and model artifact storage are encrypted with the customer key. For Private, we support wrapping keys in an HSM and provide instructions for generating and rotating keys.
00:03:00 Maya: For our compliance we need key rotation logs and proof that keys are not accessible by vendor engineers. Is that supported?
00:03:08 Alex: Yes, for customer-managed keys the cloud KMS controls access; we never store plaintext key material. Access patterns are auditable via your cloud KMS audit logs. For on-prem HSM we can produce key usage logs; and for Dedicated we can lock operator access and provide jumpbox policies — there's some implementation detail but it's a common ask.

00:03:35 Daniel: Audit logs — retention and ability to stream to our SIEM is big. We need at least 12 months retention for audit events and off-site export to Splunk or S3. What's the support?
00:03:47 Priya: We ship structured audit logs for API requests, model loads, admin actions, and key events. For Hosted, we retain logs for 90 days by default in our console but we provide an export connector to stream logs to your S3/Splunk for long-term retention. For Dedicated and Private you can set retention policies and keep logs in your own account.
00:04:10 Maya: So Hosted default 90 days — that doesn't meet 12 month requirement unless we export. Export is push or pull?
00:04:18 Priya: Export is push via event-forwarding; we can also provide a periodic batch export. We'll include our log forwarding config examples.

00:04:45 Liam: For RBAC — can we have fine-grained roles so that product teams can call hosted API but not access keys or billing?
00:04:54 Jordan: Yes, our Console supports RBAC with predefined roles and custom roles. For Hosted we have role scopes: invoice/admin, model deploy, runtime invoke, and audit-read. We also support SCIM provisioning for groups; SAML SSO for identity federation.
00:05:12 Sana: Do you support SCIM for automated group sync?
00:05:16 Priya: Yes, we support SCIM v2. You can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. For Hosted we authenticate via SAML and provision via SCIM. For Dedicated and Private you have the same SSO surface but with your IdP options bound to your tenant.

00:05:40 Daniel: Data residency — our patient data must not leave EEA for European patients. Do you have region-level hosting?
00:05:49 Alex: We offer region pinning for Hosted, i.e., process requests in specific cloud regions. For Dedicated and Private you can deploy in your VPC in the region you choose. For Hosted we currently have GCP/us-east, GCP/europe-west, AWS/eu-west regions — we'll share the region list and SLAs.

00:06:20 Maya: Related — does Redwood do any persistent storage of customer inputs for hosted? We need a clear data retention and deletion policy and the ability to purge logs and data per GDPR requests.
00:06:31 Priya: By default we keep minimal request metadata and aggregated telemetry; payloads may be logged transiently for 7 days to support debugging. We provide data deletion APIs and can perform ad-hoc wipes on request. For production healthcare usage we recommend Dedicated or Private so PII never touches our multi-tenant storage. We'll include the retention matrix in the artifacts.

00:06:55 Daniel: For Hosted, you said transient logging for 7 days — is that configurable? Can we opt out of payload logging entirely?
00:07:02 Priya: Yes, customers can opt out. The default is to keep logs for 7 days to help with debugging and rate-limit investigations, but you can disable payload persistence. For enterprise accounts we can sign SLAs around retention and deletion.

00:07:28 Liam: On the technical side — model caching and KV cache — does that ever store customer prompts that could be used by others?
00:07:37 Alex: No cross-tenant caching. KV caches are scoped to the model instance for your tenant. For Hosted we enforce strict tenant isolation at the runtime level and cannot serve cached keys to other tenants. For Dedicated/Private it's fully within your network. There are implementation details around memory encryption and zeroing which we'll document.

00:08:05 Sana: Encryption in transit — TLS? Mutual TLS?
00:08:09 Priya: All traffic is TLS1.2+ by default, we support TLS1.3. For Private and Dedicated we can support mTLS for internal service-to-service communication and client mTLS if you require it.

00:08:31 Daniel: How about developer access — debugging sessions, core dumps — can Redwood engineers access data during incident response? We need controls and audit trails.
00:08:42 Jordan: Good question. We have an access policy: vendor engineers require elevated approval, time-boxed access, and all access is audited. For Hosted we provide an access review and we can produce the audit evidence. For Dedicated/Private we can limit or remove vendor access per contract. We'll include our break-glass process.

00:09:05 Maya: Any penetration testing results or third-party assessments?
00:09:10 Alex: Yes, we have third-party pentest reports and a bug bounty program. We can share redacted pentest summaries — full reports under NDA.

00:09:28 Daniel: Regulatory — we handle PHI. Is Redwood willing to sign a BAA?
00:09:35 Jordan: For Private and Dedicated yes, we can sign a BAA. For Hosted it's negotiable and depends on deployment and controls. We'll flag legal to review.

00:09:50 Liam: On latency — if we go Dedicated, can you guarantee latency SLOs for inference?
00:09:56 Priya: Dedicated has predictable throughput and latency guarantees; we publish performance profiles per GPU type and model. For Hosted we publish median latency numbers but no hard per-customer SLO unless you move to Dedicated.

00:10:20 Maya: About network flow — if we use Hosted but require VPC peering for outbound uploads to our S3, is that possible?
00:10:29 Alex: For Hosted we don't do classic VPC peering into customer VPCs, but we support private network egress endpoints and can push files to your S3 via a VPC endpoint or use an SFTP connector. For stronger isolation use Dedicated or Private where the compute lives in your VPC.

00:10:58 Sana: Logging format — are audit logs in structured JSON with canonical fields (timestamp, actor, action, resource, outcome)? We need to be able to ingest them in our SIEM with minimal transformations.
00:11:08 Priya: Yes, audit logs are structured and include those canonical fields. We'll include sample logs in the artifacts.

00:11:35 Daniel: Bring-your-own key rotation — how often and who performs it?
00:11:39 Alex: Key rotation is managed by your KMS policy. We recommend quarterly rotation; the runtime supports key rotation without downtime using envelope encryption — we'll share the process.

00:12:00 Maya: For private deployments, are there baseline hardening scripts or CIS benchmarks?
00:12:06 Priya: We provide hardened AMIs/VM images and a deploy automation that includes CIS-like hardening, minimum port rules, and recommended OS-level configs. For on-prem we provide an ops runbook.

00:12:34 Jordan: Quick pivot — what's your timeline and procurement constraints?
00:12:38 Daniel: We're targeting a pilot in Q3, production in Q4 if security checks go well. Legal wants SOC2 evidence and a security questionnaire answered.

00:12:52 Jordan: We'll provide SOC2, ISO, pentest summary, retention matrix, and the SSO/SCIM config. We'll also propose a short POC with Dedicated nodes in eu-west.

00:13:08 Liam: Budgetary — do you have reference pricing for Dedicated?
00:13:12 Jordan: We'll include indicative pricing in the follow-ups. Pricing varies by GPU type and commitment term.

00:13:25 Sana: A couple edge questions — are model weights ever persisted unencrypted on disk during hot swaps?
00:13:33 Alex: No, weights are encrypted at rest and transiently loaded into encrypted memory; hot swaps stream from encrypted storage to memory and we zero memory on eviction. We'll include the memory handling notes.

00:13:50 Maya: If we need egress filtering to strip PHI from logs before export, do you have built-in DLP?
00:13:58 Priya: We have basic redaction heuristics and can do a pre-export hook for customers to run their DLP lambda to redact content before forwarding. For stricter controls use Dedicated or Private.

00:14:20 Daniel: For SLA/penalties around uptime and incident response — what's standard?
00:14:25 Jordan: Hosted has standard uptime commitments; Dedicated has SLA-backed targets with faster incident response and a dedicated support channel. We'll include the SLA matrix.

00:14:40 Liam: Can you summarize differences to make an informed choice?
00:14:44 Priya: Short: Hosted = fastest onboarding, managed keys by default, shorter log retention unless exported, less operational isolation. Dedicated = reserved capacity in our cloud tenant but customer-dedicated pools, supports CMK, stronger SLOs and configurable retention. Private = customer-controlled compute (VPC/on-prem), full control of keys, retention, and network, best for PHI/regulatory.

00:15:20 Daniel: Good — for our case probably Dedicated in eu-west as pilot, with options to move to Private if legal requires full on-prem.

00:15:35 Jordan: Great. We'll follow up with artifacts. Any final questions?
00:15:40 Sana: One: can you provide evidence of least-privilege access for your ops team?
00:15:46 Alex: Yes, we'll include an access control policy, sample role mappings, and audit extracts.
00:16:00 Maya: Also would like a runbook for incident containment — e.g., key compromise steps.
00:16:06 Jordan: We'll include that.

00:16:25 Liam: Thanks all.
00:16:28 Jordan: Recap of next steps: Jordan to send SOC2/ISO/pentest artifacts and pricing; Priya to share VPC/private deployment docs plus audit log forwarding examples; Alex to prepare KMS/HSM integration notes and sample terraform; schedule SE deep-dive for next Wednesday.
00:16:50 Daniel: Perfect.
00:17:00 End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional name mis-hearings (Aeon pronounced "E-on" in places), some product names transcribed as "Key M-S" instead of KMS. There are natural speech disfluencies and truncation around 00:13:xx when network blip caused partial overlap.

References mentioned: SOC2 report (will be shared), ISO 27001 cert, pentest summary (link to be provided under NDA), VPC deployment diagram (to be shared), SSO/SCIM config examples (to be shared).
